text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police fiestas were sponsored by local drug dealers before the change in government, MP tells parliament.
- Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller goes to Moscow to thwart Cyprus's purchase of the S300 missile system.
- Fuel prices are to go up.
- A basis for a solution in Cyprus is "already on the table" says Britain's minister of state David Davis.
- Civil defence bill nears end of the road.
- Communist party Akel expresses reservations over Britain's stance on the Cyprus problem.
- Twenty-five children are roaming the streets because of legal obstacles in taking on new welfare staff.
- Cypriots spent 18 million pounds on gambling in 1996.
- Cost of living is expected to shoot up from fuel increases due to come into effect from today.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash makes mediators' task difficult by insisting that Turkish occupying forces remain on the island.
